# Craft First Product Candidate Implementation Layering

> Five layers from the minimum thin vertical to one product-approval-only decision.

| Layer | Theme | Decision unlocked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `L0` | minimum thin vertical proof | a minimal Craft product vertical can connect explicit prototype meaning to one observable implementation result |
| `L1` | prototype repeatability and hardening | the full prototype spine is repeatable, deterministic, failure-aware, and ready to freeze |
| `L2` | exact product-candidate freeze | one immutable manifest completely identifies the product bytes and tests that will be judged |
| `L3` | current complete product testing | the exact frozen candidate currently passes every required product test and is eligible for product approval |
| `L4` | single product-approval checkpoint | the exact tested candidate is approved as the product result, with no operational authority inferred |

## L0 — minimum thin vertical proof

After this layer, we know whether a minimal Craft product vertical can connect explicit prototype meaning to one observable implementation result.

- Minimum working unit: Prototype Definitions, one non-authoritative navigation scaffold, and the smallest Product Capability-to-implementation slice that produces one smoke-test result.
- Included: Only one provisional capability, minimal business closure, minimal DomainSpec source, one deterministic compiled model, one implementation path, and one smoke witness.
- Deferred: Completeness, reliability hardening, candidate freeze, full product testing, product approval, and every operational effect.
- Visible outcome: An agent and reviewer can trace one intended product behavior from prototype meaning to observable output.
- Risk reduced: The architecture may be coherent on paper but incapable of producing a product result.
- Main cost drivers: Prototype schemas, generator, compiler slice, minimal implementation, and smoke-test harness.
- Exit evidence: Exact trace closure plus one reproducible smoke result and scaffold non-authority tests.
- Promotion: Continue to L1 when the thin vertical works; pivot when identities or compilation boundaries fail; stop when no useful product result can be produced.
- Non-regression: Prototype posture, identity separation, source direction, and zero authority effect remain explicit.
- Next: L1 prototype repeatability and hardening

## L1 — prototype repeatability and hardening

After this layer, we know whether the full prototype spine is repeatable, deterministic, failure-aware, and ready to freeze.

- Minimum working unit: All candidate-bound prototype stages reach TESTED_PROTOTYPE under current positive and hostile tests.
- Included: Iteration across definitions, scaffolds, product, business, DomainSpec, compiled system, implementation, profiles, residue, and rollback.
- Deferred: Immutable candidate freeze, complete product-test execution, product approval, and operations.
- Visible outcome: The same inputs repeatedly produce the same bounded product behavior and evidence.
- Risk reduced: A one-off smoke result hides drift, failure, or non-reproducible construction.
- Main cost drivers: Hostile tests, clean-run reproducibility, profile locks, rollback rehearsal, and iteration across the prototype spine.
- Exit evidence: All required prototype stages report TESTED_PROTOTYPE with current receipts and typed residue.
- Promotion: Freeze only when every candidate-bound prototype test passes and residue is explicit.
- Non-regression: The L0 observable behavior and trace closure continue to pass.
- Next: L2 exact product-candidate freeze

## L2 — exact product-candidate freeze

After this layer, we know whether one immutable manifest completely identifies the product bytes and tests that will be judged.

- Minimum working unit: One deterministic manifest containing every candidate component, generated output, environment profile, source selector, test contract, and rollback boundary.
- Included: Exact candidate closure and invalidation rules only.
- Deferred: Test outcome, approval, activation, migration, and publication.
- Visible outcome: Everyone can identify exactly which product is under test.
- Risk reduced: Tests or approval drift across changing or partially specified bytes.
- Main cost drivers: Digest closure, final candidate placement, deterministic freeze, and stale-byte detection.
- Exit evidence: Frozen manifest reproduces and rejects any changed component.
- Promotion: Run product tests only against the exact frozen manifest.
- Non-regression: All L0 and L1 tests remain attributable to exact frozen components.
- Next: L3 current product-test evidence

## L3 — current complete product testing

After this layer, we know whether the exact frozen candidate currently passes every required product test and is eligible for product approval.

- Minimum working unit: One collect-all current evidence package covering every required product-test ID for the frozen candidate.
- Included: Positive, hostile, determinism, stale-byte, rollback, and preapproval-authority-rejection tests.
- Deferred: Product approval until every required test passes and all operational effects regardless of outcome.
- Visible outcome: The Product owner receives a complete current test result for one immutable product.
- Risk reduced: Partial validation, stale evidence, or omitted failures are presented as product readiness.
- Main cost drivers: Independent test execution, clean environments, collect-all reporting, and evidence binding.
- Exit evidence: All required current outcomes are explicit; approval eligibility is true only when all are PASS.
- Promotion: Request product approval only for a fully passing current evidence package; otherwise iterate or stop.
- Non-regression: The frozen candidate does not change during testing.
- Next: L4 product approval

## L4 — single product-approval checkpoint

After this layer, we know whether the exact tested candidate is approved as the product result, with no operational authority inferred.

- Minimum working unit: One owner decision binding the exact frozen manifest and current complete product-test evidence.
- Included: Approve, reject, defer, or stop with product-approval-only effect.
- Deferred: Every authority, admission, activation, cutover, migration, publication, release, deployment, credential, destructive, and external effect.
- Visible outcome: A clear Product-owner judgment on the exact tested candidate.
- Risk reduced: Passing tests are silently treated as product approval or product approval is inflated into operational permission.
- Main cost drivers: Owner review, exact-byte binding, invalidation rules, and decision evidence.
- Exit evidence: A valid decision receipt with product-approval-only effect and empty authority-request references.
- Promotion: End product construction. Route any desired operational effect separately after approval.
- Non-regression: The approved target and evidence remain immutable; changed bytes require a new candidate, tests, and approval epoch.
- Next: none inside this chain; operational routes are separate

## Boundary

L4 ends product construction with one product-approval-only decision. Every authority, admission, activation, cutover, migration, publication, release, deployment, credential, destructive, or external effect belongs to a later separately routed workflow.
